answer: Reputation-decay cost curve. Each identity starts at a reputation nadir and earns routing priority only through sustained valid work; idle or new identities pay a rising per-message relay fee. A periodic beacon broadcasts current fee multipliers, so attackers can’t quietly stockpile cheap identities. Because cost scales with the square of simultaneous fresh identities, a whisper of coordination collapses. Spinning up N sybils costs O(N²) in relay fees plus forfeited work history.
